data.name: Yogendr
data.gender_notes: Yogendr is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Yogendra means the lord of yoga or the one who practices yoga. It is derived from the Sanskrit words yuj (to unite or join) and indra (lord or ruler). The name Yogendr carries the meaning “Discipline of Yoga” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Yogendr usually hope their child will grow to embody discipline of yoga and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for a spiritual seeker or a yogi, signifying dedication and discipline towards the spiritual path.
data.etymology: Yogendr belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Discipline of Yoga.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Yogendr total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Yogendra is deeply rooted in the ancient Indian traditions and beliefs, reflecting a connection to the practice of yoga and its rich cultural history. Yoga, an integral part of Indian heritage, has gained global recognition for its physical, mental, and spiritual benefits. Names like Yogendra contribute to preserving and promoting this ancient practice.
data.spiritual_significance: Yogendra holds spiritual significance as it denotes one's devotion and commitment to the practice of yoga. It is a reminder to constantly work towards self-realization, union with the divine, and the attainment of inner peace and enlightenment. The name Yogendra inspires the bearer to maintain a yogic lifestyle, embodying the principles of compassion, self-control, contentment, and discipline in all aspects of their life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Yogendra: The embodiment of yoga, or disciplined self-control, in one's pursuit of spiritual enlightenment and inner peace.

historical_references.reference: Yogendra Chaitanya was a 16th-century Hindu philosopher and saint who is considered a pioneer of the Bhakti movement in Bengal. He is known for his works on the Bhagavad Gita and the Srimad Bhagavatam, and for his emphasis on devotion to Krishna.

Yogendra Saraswati was a 20th-century Hindu monk and spiritual leader who founded the Divine Life Society in Rishikesh, India. He is known for his teachings on yoga, meditation, and vegetarianism, and his advocacy for simple living and high thinking.
